traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a climbing or scrambling habit with very long, slender rachises. The leaves are compound with alternate leaflets. The surrounding vegetation includes broad-leafed palms.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (paired leaflets are clearly visible attached at the same node along the rachis in multiple views)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (the leaflets are arranged in close proximity along the rachis without significant internodal gaps)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the leaf consists of multiple distinct leaflets attached to a central axis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (a single terminal leaflet is visible at the apex of the leaf structure)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 8 (visible leaflets in the best views range between 7 and 9, with an estimate of 8)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are attached along the rachis in a staggered, alternating pattern rather than directly across from one another)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaflets have smooth edges, though some physical damage/holes are present)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated and tapering towards the tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaflets taper to a distinct, elongated point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (the base of the leaflets appears broadly rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is clearly visible with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, parallel to each other, and spaced regularly along the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaflets exhibit a glossy sheen, particularly in the close-up images)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the rachis extending the leaflets is notably long and slender)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the rachis appears round and slender in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the main stem appears rigid and lignified, consistent with a woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown (the stem is a dull brownish color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears uniform without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the base of the petioles)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a climbing or scrambling habit with very long, slender rachises. The leaves are compound with alternate leaflets. The surrounding vegetation includes broad-leafed palms.
